title: Where Is Angular Used? knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Where Is Angular Used?”?
options: Where Is Angular Used? helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Where Is Angular Used? means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Where Is Angular Used? removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Where Is Angular Used? should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Where Is Angular Used? helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Where Is Angular Used? is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Business dashboards” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Business dashboards” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Business dashboards” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Business dashboards” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Business dashboards” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Business dashboards” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Business dashboards” under Where Is Angular Used?. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Where Is Angular Used?”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
